events.title: Vasco da Gama Arrives in Calicut
events.description: Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama reached Calicut on the Malabar Coast of India after sailing around the Cape of Good Hope, completing the first direct sea voyage from Europe to India.
events.significance: Opened a direct maritime trade route between Europe and Asia, launching the era of Portuguese dominance in the Indian Ocean spice trade and reshaping global commerce and colonialism.

events.title: Levi Strauss and Jacob Davis Receive Patent for Blue Jeans
events.description: Levi Strauss and tailor Jacob Davis were granted U.S. Patent No. 139,121 for using copper rivets to reinforce the stress points of work pants, creating what became blue jeans.
events.significance: The patent launched one of the most enduring garments in history, which grew from workwear into a global symbol of casual fashion and American culture.

events.title: Cuba Becomes an Independent Republic
events.description: The United States ended its military occupation of Cuba, and Tomás Estrada Palma was inaugurated as the first president of the Republic of Cuba.
events.significance: Marked formal Cuban independence after the Spanish-American War, though the Platt Amendment kept significant U.S. influence over Cuban affairs for decades.

events.title: Charles Lindbergh Begins Historic Transatlantic Flight
events.description: Charles Lindbergh took off from Roosevelt Field, New York, in the Spirit of St. Louis on the first solo nonstop transatlantic flight, landing in Paris the next day, May 21.
events.significance: Lindbergh's flight made him a global celebrity, proved the potential of long-distance air travel, and spurred rapid growth of the commercial aviation industry.

events.title: Amelia Earhart Begins Solo Transatlantic Flight
events.description: Exactly five years after Lindbergh, Amelia Earhart took off from Newfoundland in a Lockheed Vega and landed in Northern Ireland the next day, becoming the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic.
events.significance: Earhart's achievement broke gender barriers in aviation and inspired generations of women pilots.
